comment: Recorded human decisions about specific printed rows of the Consumer Council tables that the source alone cannot resolve. Each is anchored to the exact printed row it was made about and stops applying if the Council changes that row. The pipeline applies these; it never makes one. See docs/EXTRACTION.md, 'Recorded decisions'.

match.printed_tariff_name: 1 Year Home Keypad 10.5% discount plus £30 welcome credit (24hr)

decision.canonical_name: 1 Year Home Keypad 10.5% discount plus £30 welcome credit (24hr)

evidence.summary: The published name omits 'Home'. The published dataset was transcribed from the 12/09/2026 Standard table, and its own source-row trace places this product on page 6 as the third SSE row, one prepayment slot — the row that prints 'Home'. The Economy 7 sibling tariff is printed without 'Home' ('1 Year Keypad 10.5% … (E7 meter)'), which is the likely origin of the slip.

decisions.reason: Transcription correction: the printed row is the published product; its name is corrected to the source's wording and its id is kept.

products.source_discrepancy: SSE Airtricity's own Keypad tariff sheet (KEYPAD-24H-E7-2.5, V10, prices quoted from 1 August 2026) states that all Keypad customers receive a continuous 2.5% discount off the SSE Airtricity standard rate, i.e. 39.77p per kWh inc. VAT, which the Council prints separately as 'Keypad Standard 24hr 2.5%'. The Council prints 40.79p for this tariff. Transcribed as the Council prints it: the Council is the source of record, and the supplier's statement is recorded here rather than used to override it.

evidence.summary: The Council prints one row at 40.790p listing three tariff names against two payment methods with no pairing. Both 'SmartSaver Std 24hr' and 'Standard Rate 24hr' are represented in this row by the 40.79p 'Pay on receipt of bill' rate; this records no claim that they are the same product. SSE Airtricity's own sheet independently gives 40.79p as its Standard 24 Hour rate.
evidence.bullet_order: The 30/09/2026 table reorders the three names while the two methods stay in place, so bullet position is not a pairing; the decision matches the three names in any order.

supplier_documents.states: SSE Airtricity Standard, 24 Hour Home Electricity: 40.79p per kWh inc. VAT; prices quoted from 1 August 2026.
All Keypad customers get a continuous discount of 2.5% off the SSE Airtricity standard rate: 39.77p per kWh inc. VAT.

evidence.economy7_analogue: The Economy 7 table's equivalent SSE row lists two names against two methods, and a separate row gives 'Smartsaver Standard - E7' the e-bill method at the same price. Consistent with Keypad -> prepayment, but it has no 'Standard Rate 24hr' and does not settle this row.
evidence.on_receipt_ebill_not_carried: The published dataset gave 'Standard Rate 24hr' an on_receipt_ebill slot at 40.79p. No Council Standard table (12/09, 14/09 or 30/09/2026) prints that method at that rate, and SSE's sheets show no undiscounted e-bill rate. It came from the 2026-09-12 audit's judgement ('both pay-on-receipt methods'), not from the source, and is not carried.

decisions.reason: Pay on receipt of bill at 40.79p is assigned to both 'SmartSaver Std 24hr' and 'Standard Rate 24hr', which this row represents at that rate; 'Keypad Standard Rate 24hr' takes Prepayment meter as the Council prints it, with SSE's contradicting statement recorded as a source discrepancy; the unprinted on_receipt_ebill slot is not carried. The separate question of what the 1-year Keypad tariffs revert to is not decided here.
